question.text: A Cat III AIF treating listed shares as 'Stock-in-trade' means all income (capital appreciation) is taxed as:

answer.text: 'Profits and Gains from Business or Profession', irrespective of holding period

explanation.text: The Logic: Under CBDT Circular 6/2016, where a Cat III AIF treats listed shares or securities as stock-in-trade, the transfer gains are taxed as Profits and Gains from Business or Profession irrespective of the holding period. The Trap: Capital-gains treatment requires the shares to be classified as Investments. If the AIF instead opts for capital-gains treatment in a particular assessment year, it is then bound to treat such income as capital gains in subsequent assessment years. Note: Source: NISM-Series-XIX-B AIF (Cat III) Distributors workbook, pp.308-309 and 313, citing CBDT Circular 6/2016.
